subtitle: An island losing its colour

body: Paper Mario: Color Splash is a Wii U adventure set on Prism Island, where colour is being drained from the world. Mario joins Huey, a talking paint can, and searches for the missing Big Paint Stars. The paper-and-card setting makes that premise visible: damaged or empty-looking areas become invitations to restore something. Intelligent Systems builds the journey around exploration, puzzles and comic situations, using the craft materials of the world as part of its language rather than simply as a decorative treatment.

The hammer draws on a supply of red, blue and yellow paint. Filling an empty patch consumes the appropriate colour and can provide rewards; striking objects replenishes the supply. Hammer scraps increase how much Mario can carry. Another ability, Cutout, changes the route itself: tracing a dotted line on the GamePad touchscreen peels away part of the scenery and exposes a passage or secret. The island’s paper construction becomes a tool for exploration, giving Mario a way through places that initially look inaccessible.

Combat uses cards, with the Wii U GamePad involved in choosing and painting attacks. The idea carries the game’s material theme into its turn-based encounters: an action is represented by something the player handles and prepares. Color Splash places particular emphasis on the pleasure of moving through its locations and finding their comic situations. That balance distinguishes this instalment within Paper Mario’s changing approach to role-playing. Its strongest identity comes from the consistency between what the island is made of and what Mario can do to it.
